Hydrogen peroxide standards Critical: Freshly prepared sets of standards are made in tubes wrapped with aluminum foil. Prepare a 2 mM H 2 O 2 stock solution by mixing 1 μL of 4,400× H 2 O 2 with 4.4 mL of deionized water. This stock solution is used to prepare standards. See Table 2 for H 2 O 2 standard preparations with 1× PBS (Recipe 6). Table

This modification is based on the observation that the lower concentration range (0.039 μM) is not necessary for the sensitivity and detection limits of the assay under the conditions used in this study. In our sample, the free radical concentration equivalent to H 2 O 2 concentration in the standard curve fell between 10 and 20 μM. However, researchers can use lower concentrations of H 2 O 2 in the standard curve as suggested by the Abcam protocol if they use a lower number of flies or a higher dilution of fly samples.

steps.title: Prepare 1× stabilization solution
steps.instruction: Mix 550 µL of 10× stabilization reagent (from the kit) with 4 950 µL deionized water, vortex, and store at 4 °C until use (total volume ≈ 5.5 mL).

steps.title: Prepare 1× catalyst solution
steps.instruction: Combine 11 µL of 250× catalyst (from the kit) with 2 739 µL of 1× PBS (Recipe 6), vortex, and use the solution immediately.

steps.title: Prepare 1× DPS solution
steps.instruction: Mix 27.5 µL DCF‑DiOxyQ with 110 µL priming reagent, vortex, incubate at room temperature for 30 min, then add to 5 362.5 µL 1× stabilization solution, cover the tube with aluminum foil, keep on ice for immediate use (store excess at –20 °C for up to 1 week).

steps.title: Prepare 2 mM H₂O₂ stock
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of 4 400× H₂O₂ (from the kit) to 4.4 mL deionized water, vortex, and keep on ice; this stock is used for all standard preparations.

steps.title: Prepare hydrogen peroxide standards
steps.instruction: Using the 2 mM H₂O₂ stock and 1× PBS (Recipe 6), prepare eight standards as follows (keep tubes wrapped in aluminum foil):

substeps.instruction: Standard 1: 10 µL stock + 990 µL PBS → 20 µM final.
Standard 2: 500 µL Standard 1 + 500 µL PBS → 10 µM final.
Standard 3: 500 µL Standard 2 + 500 µL PBS → 5 µM final.
Standard 4: 500 µL Standard 3 + 500 µL PBS → 2.5 µM final.
Standard 5: 500 µL Standard 4 + 500 µL PBS → 1.25 µM final.
Standard 6: 500 µL Standard 5 + 500 µL PBS → 0.625 µM final.
Standard 7: 500 µL Standard 6 + 500 µL PBS → 0.313 µM final.

steps.title: Prepare 2 mg mL⁻¹ BSA stock
steps.instruction: Combine 40 µL of 50 mg mL⁻¹ BSA stock with 960 µL 1× PBS (Recipe 6) to obtain 1 000 µL of 2 mg mL⁻¹ BSA stock solution.

steps.title: Prepare BSA standards
steps.instruction: Dilute the 2 mg mL⁻¹ BSA stock in cooled 1× PBS to generate the following standards (volumes in µL):

substeps.instruction: Blank: 0 µL stock + 25 µL PBS → 0 mg mL⁻¹ (total 25 µL).
Standard 1 (0.125 mg mL⁻¹): 25 µL of 0.25 mg mL⁻¹ solution + 25 µL PBS (total 50 µL).
Standard 2 (0.25 mg mL⁻¹): 25 µL of 0.5 mg mL⁻¹ solution + 25 µL PBS (total 50 µL).
Standard 3 (0.50 mg mL⁻¹): 25 µL of 1 mg mL⁻¹ solution + 25 µL PBS (total 50 µL).
Standard 4 (1.00 mg mL⁻¹): 25 µL of 2 mg mL⁻¹ solution + 25 µL PBS (total 50 µL).
Standard 5 (2.00 mg mL⁻¹): 50 µL of 2 mg mL⁻¹ stock + 0 µL PBS (total 50 µL).

steps.title: Prepare 1× PBS buffer
steps.instruction: Make 10× PBS by dissolving 80.06 g NaCl, 2.01 g KCl, 26.8 g Na₂HPO₄, and 2.45 g KH₂PO₄ in 250 mL distilled water, adjust pH to 7.4, bring volume to 500 mL, aliquot into five 100 mL bottles, autoclave 30 min at 121 °C, then dilute 1:10 with distilled water (e.g., 50 mL 10× + 450 mL water) to obtain 1× PBS.

steps.title: Rinse and collect flies
steps.instruction: In a 9‑well glass plate, rinse 25 anesthetized flies per biological replicate with 500 µL cold 1× PBS to remove food residues.

steps.title: Homogenize flies
steps.instruction: Transfer the rinsed flies to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, spin 5 s in a tabletop mini‑centrifuge, remove all liquid with a Pasteur pipette, add 500 µL ice‑cold 1× PBS, grind with a PolyPestle, then gently pipette the lysate 5–10 times (motor optional).

steps.title: Clarify homogenate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 10 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, then transfer the ~350 µL supernatant to a new tube (keep on ice).

steps.title: Dilute supernatant
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL ice‑cold 1× PBS to 50 µL supernatant (4‑fold dilution), mix thoroughly, and either proceed immediately or store at –80 °C for up to 1 week (keep samples on ice throughout).

steps.title: Load ROS/RNS assay plate
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 µL of each diluted sample or hydrogen‑peroxide standard (in duplicate) into the wells of a clear‑bottom black 96‑well plate as per the desired layout; ensure all reagents have equilibrated to room temperature for ≥30 min.

steps.title: Add catalyst to assay wells
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 1× catalyst to each well containing sample or standard, then gently pipette to mix.

steps.title: Incubate after catalyst addition
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 5 min to allow reaction with the catalyst.

steps.title: Add DPS solution
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 1× DPS to each well, cover the plate with aluminum foil to protect from light.

steps.title: Develop fluorescence
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 45 min for fluorescence development.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Using the Agilent BioTek Synergy H1 plate reader, set excitation to 480 nm and emission to 530 nm, then read fluorescence of each well; if any sample exceeds the highest standard, dilute in PBS and re‑measure.

steps.title: Prepare BSA standard plate
steps.instruction: Dispense 5 µL of each BSA standard solution twice (2 × 5 µL) into the appropriate wells of a clear‑bottom 96‑well plate according to the layout (Table 5).

steps.title: Add samples for protein assay
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of each diluted fly homogenate sample (in duplicate) to the designated wells of a transparent 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Add Bradford reagent
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of Bradford reagent (room temperature) to every well containing a BSA standard or sample, mix by pipetting five times, and seal the plate with parafilm.

steps.title: Incubate Bradford reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the sealed plate at room temperature for 30 min.

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Read absorbance at 595 nm on the BioTek Synergy H1 plate reader; average duplicate readings, subtract the mean blank, and use the BSA standard curve to calculate protein concentrations.

steps.title: Set up plate reader software
steps.instruction: Power on the Synergy H1, launch Gen5 3.14 software, allow initialization and calibration, create a new read, define the plate layout, select Fluorescence (480 nm/530 nm) or Absorbance (595 nm) as needed, place the plate in the holder, click Read, then export or save the data for analysis.

description: Validation of protocol Figure 2 demonstrates typical results of assays quantifying ROS/RNS free radicals and Figure 3 demonstrates the result of the assay for protein quantification. Fluorescence measurement was performed on the Agilent BioTek synergy H1 plate reader. Use a 480/530 nm filter set with a 530 nm cutoff. The data provided is solely for reference and should not be used to interpret actual results. Figure 2. Standard curve of hydrogen peroxide Figure 3. Standard curve for protein quantification
